Circle areas are proportional to parameter counts, and the shaded band marks real-time generation. Video results can be found atkyutai.org/aura.

Figure 3:Two-stage distillation pipeline.Stage 1 (top, ODE teacher forcing): the frozen teacher generates a multi-step ODE trajectory from noise to clean latents, conditioned on a reference image, speech audio, and text prompt. Aper-chunk mixed timestepstate is sampled from this trajectory and fed to the causal studentGθG_{\theta}, which is trained to predict the corresponding clean latents under an MSE loss.Stage 2 (bottom, DMD with backward simulation): the student generates a video in inference mode without gradients (backward simulation, left), and a per-chunk mixed-timestep state is sampled from its own denoising trajectory. The student is then re-run on this state with gradients enabled, and a DMD loss is computed by comparing the score predicted by a frozen teacher and an online fake score network (right). Gradients flow back through the gradient-enabled student pass only.

Figure 5:Qualitative results from AURAon two diverse test sequences with different audios, generated by AURA 5B (top) and AURA 1.3B (bottom). Figure 9:Qualitative comparison on the Hallo3 test set. Despite stronger FID/FVD scores (Table1), Hallo3 generations exhibit recurrent hand artifacts (bottom) that distribution-based metrics fail to penalize. AURA (top) produces cleaner outputs at a fraction of the generation time.

Figure 10:Qualitative comparison between AURA 5B and its TalkVerse teacher. Given the same reference image (left) and a1010s audio input, AURA 5B (bottom) generates video of comparable visual quality to the teacher (top) while running approximately17×17\timesfaster end-to-end on a single H100 GPU.
